clue.text: Reflected sound needed by college choirs

indicators.note: what is needed by a group is held within it, so the answer sits inside the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the join between the two words

explanation.surface: A college choir relies on a resonant chapel to make its singing ring out.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer straddles colleg-E CHO-irs; choirs and reflected sound make the hiding place feel natural.
explanation.definitionFit: An echo is the repeat of a noise bounced back off a wall or cliff, a simple synonym.

clue.text: International trader's former carrier

parts.note: an ex is a former partner, so EX means former
a porter carries luggage

explanation.surface: A merchant who trades abroad once worked as a luggage carrier.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sells goods to buyers in other countries is engaged in commerce across borders.

clue.text: Meat and veg dish's hot remains

parts.note: H is the standard abbreviation for hot, as on taps
ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: Leftovers from a hot stew of meat and vegetables are still warm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remains' reads as leftover food, but it means the residue of a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Hash is a dish of chopped cooked meat fried with potatoes and other vegetables.

clue.text: Charm we recalled, feeding female dog

indicators.note: food goes into the one being fed, so this piece is put inside the other

parts.note: a bitch is a female dog

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the letters go backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: We remember the charming way we used to feed the dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' suggests memory but asks for a turnaround of WE.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to charm someone is to captivate or enchant them, as if by magic spell.

clue.text: Forbidden woman entering base

indicators.note: to enter is to go into something, so one piece goes inside another

explanation.surface: A woman has been barred from entering a military base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Base' suggests a military camp but is a foundation or bottom layer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something forbidden has been prohibited by an official rule, the same as outlawed.

clue.text: Jazzman in central London with a big tree

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it is placed inside it

parts.note: W1 is the postcode of the West End of London, with the 1 read as I
Duke Ellington was a great jazz bandleader
taken as written

explanation.surface: A jazz musician in the West End is accompanied by a huge tree.
explanation.walkthrough: London postcodes are a crossword staple: W1 covers central London's West End, and the digit 1 doubles as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Wellingtonia is the British name for the giant sequoia, an enormous redwood conifer from California.

clue.text: Urban dweller in Kent finally has staff

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so only the closing letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the final letter of Kent
to have something is to own it
to staff a post is to man it

explanation.surface: A city resident living in Kent finally has some employees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' looks like a noun for employees but is the verb meaning to provide people for. Kent is an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: A townsman lives in a town rather than the countryside, so he is a city or town resident.

clue.text: Group of beasts tried to be listened to

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tried' is the legal sense: a judge has heard the case.
explanation.definitionFit: A herd is a large group of cattle or other animals that feed and travel together.

clue.text: Unpleasant ride a beagle's suffering

indicators.note: something suffering is in a bad state, knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange, including the s

explanation.surface: Riding while a hunting dog is in pain is an unpleasant experience.
explanation.walkthrough: The s of the possessive is part of the letters to shuffle; a beagle is a small hunting hound.
explanation.definitionFit: Something disagreeable is not to one's liking, offensive or nasty in manner or effect.

clue.text: Overtake one on river, blooming thing

parts.note: to pass a car is to overtake it
I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written
a river is something that flows, a flow-er

explanation.surface: A driver overtakes someone on a river road, cursing the 'blooming' slowcoach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'River' as FLOWER, something that flows, is an old crossword joke; 'blooming' also passes for a mild British oath.
explanation.definitionFit: The passion flower is a climbing plant with striking blooms, so it is literally a thing that blooms.

clue.text: Feller's tool unknown by a European

x is the classic unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.walkthrough: 'By' means beside, so the unknown sits beside A and E, between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A feller is someone who cuts down trees, and an axe is the chopping implement for that job.

clue.text: Leather strap Republican removed from crowd

parts.note: a throng is a large crowd
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A Republican politician is ejected from a crowd, perhaps by someone wielding a strap.
explanation.walkthrough: Take R out of THRONG to leave THONG.
explanation.definitionFit: A thong is a narrow strip of leather used as a lace, whip or fastening.

clue.text: Revealed son carrying mail for distant territories

parts.note: a secret that is revealed is out
post is the British word for mail
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A son is exposed as carrying letters to far-flung colonies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carrying' places the son behind the mail he bears, so S follows POST rather than wrapping it.
explanation.definitionFit: Outposts are remote settlements or stations far from the centre of an empire.

clue.text: Forceful, backing a lot in police department

explanation.definitionFit: A dynamic person is energetic and vigorous, full of drive and positive energy.

clue.text: Building material originally common on Greek island

parts.note: the first letter of common
taken as written
Crete is the largest Greek island

explanation.definitionFit: Concrete is a mix of cement, sand, gravel and water used in construction.

clue.text: Engineers negotiate withdrawal

explanation.surface: Army engineers negotiate a pull-out of troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Treat' in its older sense of bargaining, as in a treaty.

clue.text: Sign a chap's dropped from word book

clue.text: A board game in the past

go is an ancient Asian board game

clue.text: Disobedient brat involved with union side

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

clue.text: She entertains great numbers outside quarters
